sections.h2: Sale routes for an Aventura owner
sections.html:
In a condominium town, the building adds a step to every route: an agent, a private deal or a cash buyer. The city describes itself as an upscale condo community with large, well-known condominium and apartment buildings.

Before choosing, gather your association's documents and ask what approvals a buyer needs. Cash skips lender rules, though an association may still screen the buyer.

  • Through an agent: financed buyers and association approvals.
  • Directly: you arrange the contract and closing agent.
  • For cash: a closing day that suits your move.

Aventura covers 3.2 square miles on the Intracoastal Waterway in northeast Miami-Dade County, and it was incorporated in 1995. Downtown Fort Lauderdale and Miami are about 20 minutes away, and Aventura Mall, restaurants and theaters are close by.

Those travel times are worth mentioning in a listing, since buyers often weigh waterfront access and commute together.

sections.h2: Miami-Dade property tax and an Aventura sale
sections.html:
The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser values property but doesn't send tax bills or set taxes. Questions about a bill go to the Miami-Dade Tax Collector. The appraiser's office takes calls at 305-375-4712, and applications for widow and widower exemptions and for veteran disability exemptions can be filed online.

The yearly sequence is steady. The appraiser releases estimates of taxable value on June 1, sends a preliminary certification to the taxing authorities on July 1, and certifies the roll in the fall. Because values reflect January 1 conditions, a change of ownership shows up in assessed value on the next January 1 and in the bill that follows.

Ask the Tax Collector for a current-year balance so the closing statement matches the roll. Keep the August notice of proposed taxes with your closing papers, since it shows how each taxing authority proposed to set its rate.

Who does what for an Aventura owner
OfficeRole
Property AppraiserValues parcels and approves exemptions
Tax CollectorMails the bill and takes payment
Clerk and ComptrollerRecords deeds and runs an alert service against deed fraud
Value Adjustment BoardHears value petitions, filed within 25 days of the August notice

Homestead relief reaches $50,000 of value for owners who applied by March 1. Save Our Homes keeps annual assessment growth at or under inflation, never above 3 percent, and the state's 2026 figure is 2.7 percent.

Any change in title resets the property to market value on the next January 1, so your buyer's first bill may look much higher than yours. Portability can carry part of your savings to a new Florida homestead set up inside a three year window. Renting the unit or moving out ends the homestead, so avoid a long rental between listing and closing.

Other benefits may matter to you or to your buyer. An ordinance may give owners 65 or older an added homestead exemption of up to $50,000 within an income limit. A disabled ex-servicemember may receive a $5,000 reduction in assessed value, and a veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability may receive a homestead discount equal to the VA disability percentage. Ask the Miami-Dade Property Appraiser which of these apply to the unit.

Bills arrive in November, discounted 4 percent at first and 1 percent by February, and unpaid ones go delinquent April 1.

Miami-Dade stands apart on deed tax: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that doesn't apply to a document moving only a single-family dwelling. Other counties charge 70 cents.

Every party to the deed answers to the state for the tax, so the contract should name who covers it. The surtax exception is worded for single-family dwellings, so ask the clerk or your closing agent how a condominium unit is treated before you price the sale. Recording charges at the clerk are set by statute per page. Deeds need two subscribing witnesses.

A Department of Revenue advisement found that one lady bird deed conveyed no present beneficial interest and so carried no deed tax. It rests on its own facts, so get advice before using one.

The Miami-Dade clerk runs a no-cost alert system that emails you within 24 hours of a deed or mortgage being filed under your name. Separately, the appraiser's compliance staff accept homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

Owners of a vacant unit should enroll and keep a current mailing address on file.

The appraiser has offices in downtown Miami and at the South Dade Government Center in Cutler Bay, and appointments can be booked online. Bring the deed and any exemption paperwork if you need a record corrected before closing.

Start with the building. Ask the association for its financial statements, pending assessments and approval rules, then compare the price against what the appraiser shows for the folio. The property record lists assessments, exemptions and sales, and the appraiser's tax estimator tutorial explains how a buyer can estimate a bill.

  • Payoff letters from every lender or lien holder on the unit.
  • Proof of exemptions you hold, since a sale ends the homestead on that unit.
  • The contract clause naming who pays deed tax.
  • The Tax Collector's balance for this year.

Other situations change the schedule. A renter behind on payments can be served a written three day notice that skips weekends and court holidays. After a foreclosure judgment the auction follows in 20 to 35 days. A small estate, one at or under $150,000, can use summary administration. Speak with a Florida attorney early about any of these.

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens the file. Send it your deed, association contact and loan payoff information right away. If the association requires approval or a statement of dues, request it the same day, because associations often take longest to reply.

Before closing, read the settlement statement for the payoff, tax credit, deed tax and any dues owed to the association. Ask about a final meter reading, keys, fobs and parking or storage items that go with the unit. A cash buyer shortens the path by skipping loan underwriting, but the title work, deed recording and tax settlement still happen in the same order.

faqs.q: Who sends an Aventura property tax bill?
faqs.a: The Miami-Dade Tax Collector mails it. The appraiser's role stops at valuation.

faqs.q: What deed tax applies to an Aventura sale?
faqs.a: Miami-Dade charges 60 cents per $100 and adds a 45 cents per $100 surtax that skips single-family dwelling transfers. Ask the clerk whether a condo unit counts.

faqs.q: When did Aventura become a city?
faqs.a: Aventura was incorporated in 1995. It covers 3.2 square miles on the Intracoastal Waterway in northeast Miami-Dade County.

faqs.q: Can a cash buyer purchase an Aventura condo as is?
faqs.a: Often, but an association may screen buyers, so read your documents and ask the board before fixing a closing day.

faqs.q: How can I guard against deed fraud while selling?
faqs.a: Enroll in the clerk's free alert, which messages you within 24 hours after any deed or mortgage is filed in your name.
